## Description
 &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;Use blown film extrusion with the following steps:&#10;&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;1. Extrusion: Polyethylene resin pellets are melted and forced through a &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;   circular die to form a continuous tube. &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;2. Inflation: Air is pumped into the molten plastic, inflating it into a &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;   thin, balloon-like film bubble to stretch it to the desired thickness. &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;3. Cooling and Flattening: The film is cooled, flattened using nip rollers, &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;   and wound into large rolls. &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;4. Conversion: The film is cut, heat-sealed, and printed to create the final&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;   bag shape. &#10;&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;To further enhance durability, manufacturers may add plasticizers, stabilizers, &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;UV inhibitors, and mineral fillers (like calcium carbonate) to the resin &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;before extrusion.&#10;&#9;&#9;
